======================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Jitendra Narain Sinha
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Md. Fahimuddin
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Chakradhari
 Sharan Singh
 Oral Order
2 05-09-2016
Heard learned Counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

This application, for grant of anticipatory bail, arises out of G. O. Case No. 69 of 2006, disclosing offences under Sections 2 (ix) (j) (k) and 7 (h) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1955, and Rules 50 (1) and 32 (b) (e) (f) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rule, 2004.

Allegedly, from the shop of one Sitaram Choudhary, at Darbhanga, certain food item (chanachur)
was seized, which was found to be misbranded.
He is said to have disclosed the Food Inspector that supply of the said food item was made by the petitioner.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that only on the basis of the statement of the co- accused, petitioner has been named in the First Information Report.
He has also submitted that there is no allegation of adulteration made in the First Information Report.

According to him, if the petitioner is granted anticipatory bail, there would be no chance of tampering with the evidence or petitioner fleeing from the course of investigation, considering the nature of allegation made in the prosecution report.
Considering the above submission, this application is allowed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Let the petitioner, Kedar Sao, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the Court below within six weeks, be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate,
Darbhanga, in connection with G. O. Case No. 69 of 2006, subject to the condition laid down under Section 438 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

This is subject to the condition that the petitioner shall present himself before the police/Court, as the case may be, as and when required and in the event of failure on his part to appear before the Court on two consecutive occasions, his bail bond shall be liable to be cancelled.

(Chakradhari Sharan Singh, J.) Prabhakar Anand/-
